chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl from al-Abbas ibn Amir from Aban ibn Uthman from Mansur ibn Hazim said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a woman and does not specify a dowry for her. He said, 'She has nothing of the dowry. But if he has consummated the marriage with her, then she is entitled to the dowry of her peers.'

key_terms.مَهْرُ نِسَائِهَا: dowry of her peers (standard dowry for women of similar status)

ai.seo_question: What is the dowry entitlement for a wife if no specific amount was agreed upon at the time of marriage?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the default dowry mechanism when no specific amount is agreed upon, establishing 'mahr al-nisā' (the dowry of her peers) as the entitlement upon consummation. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle that consummation validates the right to compensation even in the absence of a written or verbal contract, reflecting the practical application of justice in marital contracts. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how implicit agreements are interpreted within the framework of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
